catalyst_text: Presented positive Phase 3 SLE data at EULAR
detailed_catalyst_text: Phase 3 PHOENYCS GO results in systemic lupus erythematosus were presented at EULAR 2026, showing sustained disease control with reduced glucocorticoid use, improvements in immunologic markers, and reduced flares through Week 48. The results were also recently published in The Lancet, reporting clinically meaningful improvements and a generally favorable safety profile. These findings support the potential for steroid-sparing disease control in SLE.
catalyst_text_evidence: UCB (Euronext Brussels: UCB) and Biogen Inc. (NASDAQ:BIIB) today announced data, comprising two posters and three abstracts, at the European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (EULAR) 2026 Congress, demonstrating the clinical profile of dapirolizumab pegol (DZP), an investigational biologic in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). Post hoc analyses displayed in one of the posters from the PHOENYCS GO program showed that, in patients with baseline glucocorticoid dose >7.5 mg/day prednisone equivalent, treatment with DZP plus standard of care was associated with a higher proportion of patients achieving control of disease activity while enabling glucocorticoid tapering to ≤7.5 mg/day through Week 48, compared with placebo plus standard of care. Additional EULAR 2026 presentations highlighted the breadth of data from the PHOENYCS GO program, including: Improvements in key immunological markers, including reduced anti-dsDNA antibodies and increased complement proteins C3 and C4 in patients with abnormal levels at baseline (Poster POS1364). Lower rates of moderate or moderate/severe BILAG-2004 flares with DZP plus standard of care versus placebo plus standard of care through Week 48, using alternative definitions of flares to increase measurement sensitivity (Abstract AB1163). The EULAR data follow the recent publication of the Phase 3 PHOENYCS GO study in The Lancet, reporting clinically meaningful improvements in disease activity with dapirolizumab pegol at Week 48.

catalyst_text: Received FDA Breakthrough Therapy Designation for SMA
detailed_catalyst_text: FDA granted Breakthrough Therapy Designation for an investigational therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, supported by exploratory Phase 1b data in children with suboptimal response to prior gene therapy. The program includes multiple Phase 3 studies with two recruiting, underscoring advancement into late-stage development.
catalyst_text_evidence: Biogen Inc. (NASDAQ:BIIB) announced today that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has granted salanersen Breakthrough Therapy Designation for the treatment of spinal muscular atrophy (SMA). The salanersen Phase 3 program consists of three global studies: STELLAR-1 (recruiting), an open-label study, will evaluate the effects of salanersen in young (under 6 weeks old), treatment-naïve and clinically presymptomatic infants with a genetic diagnosis of SMA SOLAR (recruiting), an open-label study, will evaluate the effects of salanersen in teens and adults (aged 15–60 years) with SMA who are either treatment-naïve or previously treated with risdiplam STELLAR-2 (recruitment expected to begin in June 2026), a randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled study, will evaluate the effects of salanersen when initiated ~6 months after onasemnogene abeparvovec-xioi in infants with SMA who received presymptomatic treatment with gene therapy at 6 weeks of age or younger

catalyst_text: Announced negative topline results from Phase 2b trial
detailed_catalyst_text: Topline data from the Phase 2b LUMA study in early-stage Parkinson's disease showed no slowing of disease progression versus placebo on the primary endpoint and no benefit on secondary endpoints. Exploratory biomarker analyses indicated robust peripheral LRRK2 kinase inhibition and acceptable safety, but efficacy was not demonstrated.
catalyst_text_evidence: Biogen Inc. (NASDAQ:BIIB) and Denali Therapeutics Inc. (NASDAQ:DNLI) today announced topline results from the Phase 2b LUMA study evaluating BIIB122 (DNL151), an investigational small molecule inhibitor of LRRK2 (leucine-rich repeat kinase 2), in individuals with early-stage Parkinson's disease. Results from the study show that BIIB122 did not slow the progression of Parkinson's disease versus placebo, as measured by the primary endpoint of Time to Confirmed Worsening in the modified Movement Disorder Society Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale (MDS-UPDRS) Part II and III combined score. Secondary endpoints also did not show a benefit with BIIB122.

catalyst_text: Announced positive topline Phase 2 results in early Alzheimers
detailed_catalyst_text: Topline results from a randomized Phase 2 study in early Alzheimer’s disease showed robust reductions in CSF tau and tau PET, with pre-specified analyses indicating slowed clinical decline, especially at the lowest dose. Although the dose-response primary endpoint on CDR-SB at Week 76 was not met, the biomarker and clinical signals support advancement toward registrational development.
catalyst_text_evidence: CAMBRIDGE, Mass., 2026-05-14 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Biogen Inc. (NASDAQ:BIIB) today announced compelling topline results from the Phase 2 CELIA study evaluating diranersen (BIIB080), an investigational antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) therapy targeting tau, in individuals with early Alzheimer's disease. Pre-specified analyses of cognitive endpoints demonstrated slowing of clinical decline across all studied doses, particularly in participants receiving the lowest dose of diranersen, 60 mg administered every 24 weeks. Diranersen also demonstrated robust reductions in both cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) tau and tau pathology, as measured by positron emission tomography (PET), across all studied doses, with reductions maintained throughout the dosing period. CELIA did not meet its primary endpoint assessing dose response for change from baseline on the Clinical Dementia Rating–Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB) at Week 76.

catalyst_text: Received FDA approval for high dose regimen
detailed_catalyst_text: The FDA approved a high dose regimen of nusinersen (50 mg loading and 28 mg maintenance) for the treatment of spinal muscular atrophy. The decision was supported by the pivotal Phase 2/3 DEVOTE study demonstrating significant motor function improvements in treatment‑naïve infants. This approval provides an additional dosing option intended to better address patient needs across SMA.
catalyst_text_evidence: Biogen Inc. (NASDAQ:BIIB) today announced that the High Dose Regimen of SPINRAZA (nusinersen), which is comprised of 50 mg/5 mL and 28 mg/5 mL doses, was approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for the treatment of spinal muscular atrophy (SMA). The FDA approval is based on data from the three-part, Phase 2/3 DEVOTE study.

catalyst_text: Received FDA Breakthrough Therapy Designation for indication
detailed_catalyst_text: The FDA granted Breakthrough Therapy Designation to litifilimab for cutaneous lupus erythematosus. The designation was supported by results from Part A (Phase 2) of the AMETHYST study along with previously presented Phase 2 LILAC data, indicating potential benefit in this population. This designation may expedite development and review for a disease with no targeted treatments.
catalyst_text_evidence: Earlier this year, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration granted litifilimab Breakthrough Therapy Designation for CLE. Results from the Phase 2 (Part A) part of the AMETHYST study supported the designation, in addition to the previously presented Phase 2 LILAC study results.

catalyst_text: Reported positive Phase 1b and initiated Phase 3
detailed_catalyst_text: New Phase 1b results in children with spinal muscular atrophy were presented, showing salanersen was generally well tolerated with reductions in neurodegeneration markers and functional improvements, including new WHO motor milestones. Additionally, the Phase 3 program has begun, with the STELLAR-1 study initiating screening. These milestones advance the program into late-stage evaluation across the SMA population.
catalyst_text_evidence: Biogen Inc. (NASDAQ:BIIB) presented additional results from the Phase 1b study of salanersen, an investigational novel antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) given once a year for spinal muscular atrophy (SMA), at the 2026 Muscular Dystrophy Association (MDA) Clinical & Scientific Conference. Salanersen was generally well-tolerated. Participants experienced a slowing of neurodegeneration and functional improvement, including achievement of new World Health Organization (WHO) motor milestones, following initiation of salanersen. These new results include a minimum of one year of follow-up for all participants, building on the interim study data presented at Cure SMA 2025. The clinical development program has already commenced with STELLAR-1 initiated screening, and the other studies planned to initiate in Q2 2026 (SOLAR) and Q3 2026 (STELLAR-2).

catalyst_text: China BLA accepted and granted priority review designation
detailed_catalyst_text: China’s regulator accepted the biologics license application for the subcutaneous autoinjector formulation and has granted Priority Review. The submission covers a once‑weekly subcutaneous option for Alzheimer’s disease as an alternative to biweekly IV administration. Priority Review in China is intended to shorten the assessment period, underscoring the therapy’s clinical value.

catalyst_text: sBLA accepted Priority Review PDUFA May 24 2026
detailed_catalyst_text: The FDA accepted the supplemental biologics license application for a weekly subcutaneous autoinjector starting dose in early Alzheimer’s disease and granted Priority Review with a PDUFA date of 2026-05-24. The submission seeks to enable at-home initiation dosing as an alternative to bi-weekly IV infusions. This could broaden patient access and streamline treatment by offering subcutaneous administration from initiation through maintenance.
